title: Adaptive glass legibility — the backdrop-luminance bucket that DARKENS the glass over light/busy backdrops to a bounded AA floor (the iOS-26/27 locally-darken move)
defect: G2 — Glass dock over VERY LIGHT materials is unreadable; dynamically darken the glass adaptively. SOTA as of iOS 27.
head: da57287
headNote: W54 glass-first CSS core + the --glass-level scalar already landed; W54 routed --glass-bg-dock through the oklab tint seam at --glass-tint-strength:0 (zero-delta). W44 dark-arm edits preserved.

ratifiedDefaults.morphRootInterp: resting-endpoint-only (the morph interp stays color-mix(in srgb …); the adaptive darken rides --glass-bg-dock at the resting endpoint)
ratifiedDefaults.aaBandCeiling: 18% (clamped LOW by the live readback — the lowest value that clears 4.5:1 over synthetic white; ≤24% translucency floor; measured ~11:1 card / ~17:1 dock at 18%, well above the floor, headroom kept)
ratifiedDefaults.numericLumaObserver: demo-private (the token is minted; the JS observer ships only with ≥2 consumers — the no-overfitting bar)
ratifiedDefaults.glassLevelPlaceholder: W54's --glass-level is LANDED at HEAD; no placeholder needed — the a11y brackets already ride it (W54 collapsed them), W55 adds the tint-axis coordination
ratifiedDefaults.contrastColorAnchor: contrast-color(var(--card)) — anchored on the LIGHT backdrop signal (over the light backdrop → the legible dark ink); NOT contrast-color(var(--glass-tint-ink)) which inverts to white (illegible on the still-light plate). The LIVE readback caught this — the dark-ink anchor gave 1.56:1; the card anchor gives the dark-text 13.5:1.
